accounted.item: One item on a private person

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/The papers in print, the bar and the choice (X-1787-00)
accounted.item: The papers in print, the bar and the choice (X-1787-00)
accounted.note: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended, B1) with 7 papers (10 catalogue series, C-04): 4 in print from January to April, 3 in May and June, 6 from September; an item is eligible in 4 papers.

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/Choosing among the eligible items (X-1787-01)
accounted.item: Choosing among the eligible items (X-1787-01)
accounted.note: B1: three items printed by every paper in print are admitted; 10 others are chosen; the Philadelphia paragraph on Mr. Gerry and Mr. Mason, of the affair of the Constitution in the same weeks, is listed as not chosen (X-1800-01).

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/Pages filed under another date (X-1787-02)
accounted.item: Pages filed under another date (X-1787-02)
accounted.note: Printings on pages filed under another date keep the release's page keys and carry notes with the printed dates.

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/Private persons (X-1787-03)
accounted.item: Private persons (X-1787-03)
accounted.note: One eligible item turns on a private person; it is not chosen and is listed for the owner without names (R-04).

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/Advertisements and legal notices (X-1787-04)
accounted.item: Advertisements and legal notices (X-1787-04)
accounted.note: Advertisements, legal notices and formulas over the bar are not news items and are not counted (C-10); they are listed by count.

accounted.source: stories_1787.json#for_user_decision/The Federalist (X-1787-05)
accounted.item: The Federalist (X-1787-05)
accounted.note: The Federalist's numbers of 1787 stand in 3 papers each, below the bar; they are listed as one line.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/The papers in print and the bar (X-1788-00)
accounted.item: The papers in print and the bar (X-1788-00)
accounted.note: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended, B1) with 6 papers and 4 or 5 in print in an item's weeks: an item is eligible in 4 papers all year.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Choosing among the eligible items (X-1788-01)
accounted.item: Choosing among the eligible items (X-1788-01)
accounted.note: B1: the one item printed by every paper that survives for its weeks is admitted; the 6 other eligible news items are all chosen (7 stories); the 6 notices and advertisements are not chosen (C-10).

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Another text that shares the words (X-1788-02)
accounted.item: Another text that shares the words (X-1788-02)
accounted.note: North Carolina's declaration of rights and amendments is not a printing of Virginia's amendments (C-07); Virginia's amendments are in 3 papers by their opening and are listed below the rule.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/A paragraph counted by its own words (X-1788-03)
accounted.item: A paragraph counted by its own words (X-1788-03)
accounted.note: The London paragraph on letters from Algiers is one item in two forms, in 3 papers by its own words (C-02), and is listed below the rule.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Printed again counts again (X-1788-04)
accounted.item: Printed again counts again (X-1788-04)
accounted.note: The Daily Advertiser printed the French act twice (10 April, 21 May) and the journal of Congress on Kentucky twice (19 June, 19 July); each printing is in its group (C-08).

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/The ratifications of the Constitution (X-1788-05)
accounted.item: The ratifications of the Constitution (X-1788-05)
accounted.note: Only Virginia's act of ratification reaches 4 papers. The ratifications of Massachusetts, New Hampshire and New York, Virginia's amendments and the extracts from the journal of Congress of 2 and 3 June are below the bar by their opening (counts that reached another state's form were read and corrected) and are listed below the rule.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Headings above an item (X-1788-06)
accounted.item: Headings above an item (X-1788-06)
accounted.note: An excerpt starts with the heading or date line printed directly above the item; a paper's own dateline over its column, or the dateline of the paper an act was taken from, stays out of an act's or a letter's excerpt and is noted.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Notices and titles of the items not chosen (X-1788-07)
accounted.item: Notices and titles of the items not chosen (X-1788-07)
accounted.note: Eligible notices and an advertisement are not chosen (C-10) and are described without the private persons they name (R-04).

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Filing and dates (X-1788-08)
accounted.item: Filing and dates (X-1788-08)
accounted.note: The Kentucke Gazette's pages are filed as edition 2; the 10 misfiled RevX pages of 1788 hold no printing of the ledger.

accounted.source: stories_1788.json#for_user_decision/Grading calls on the transcriptions (X-1788-09)
accounted.item: Grading calls on the transcriptions (X-1788-09)
accounted.note: How the scan check graded some transcription errors (C-14), as the README says.

accounted.source: stories_1789.json#for_user_decision/The floor of four papers before 18 August
accounted.item: The floor of four papers before 18 August
accounted.note: 1789 has four papers and the fourth survives only from 18 August, so an item reaches the bar of 4 only if that paper still prints it after that day; the items printed by all three papers that survive before then are below the bar and listed here.

accounted.source: stories_1789.json#for_user_decision/The amendments to the Constitution
accounted.item: The amendments to the Constitution
accounted.note: The amendments both Houses proposed to the states and the House's articles of 24 August are counted apart, by their own words; each is listed here, below the rule.

accounted.source: stories_1789.json#for_user_decision/A report inside a longer paragraph
accounted.item: A report inside a longer paragraph
accounted.note: A report that stands inside a longer dated paragraph is counted by its own opening sentence; the report before it in the Vienna paragraph is listed here, below the rule.

accounted.source: stories_1789.json#for_user_decision/The proceedings of the House
accounted.item: The proceedings of the House
accounted.note: The House's proceedings are runs of a day's business and are not admitted; the two days printed by all four papers are listed here under digests.

accounted.source: stories_1790.json#for_user_decision/The choice under the amended rule (B1)
accounted.item: The choice under the amended rule (B1)
accounted.note: The two eligible items not printed by every surviving paper are chosen, since the year has only five eligible items; no eligible item is left out.

accounted.source: stories_1790.json#for_user_decision/An anecdote admitted by the first part
accounted.item: An anecdote admitted by the first part
accounted.note: A story told for amusement, printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, is admitted by the rule's first part, as 1793's sea serpent stood.

accounted.source: stories_1790.json#for_user_decision/The floor of four papers from August to October
accounted.item: The floor of four papers from August to October
accounted.note: From mid-August to October only three papers survive, so items printed by all three of them are below the bar of 4; those read are listed here.

accounted.source: stories_1790.json#for_user_decision/The proceedings of the House
accounted.item: The proceedings of the House
accounted.note: The House's proceedings are runs of a day's business and are not admitted; the day printed by all four papers is listed here under digests.
